name: Chromosome Spread
desc: A metaphase chromosome spread, the classic cytogenetics image: condensed chromosomes scattered across the slide, each a pair of sister chromatids pinched at a centromere into the familiar X and striped along its arms with a G-banding pattern. On the wet slide they never sit still -- each jiggles with Brownian rotation while the whole spread drifts slowly, and every few seconds a fresh metaphase is captured as all the chromosomes ease to a new scatter and settle, a perpetual re-drop that never converges. Offered as spectral karyotyping with every chromosome a vivid colour, bright-field Giemsa banding, DAPI fluorescence, or sorted into a ranked karyotype chart.

scale.doc: magnification - chromosomes swell, guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: jiggle, drift and how often a fresh metaphase re-drops
